Turtle Cottage Is a 41-ft Tiny Home With a Wooden Deck, Catpatio, and a Surprising Amount of Storage
20 photos
Photo: Tiny House Giant Journey/YouTube screenshot
Some people who decide to move into a tiny house prefer to place their new dwelling on private land and live independently, while others would rather have it parked in a tiny home community where they can enjoy shared gathering spaces and gardens to combat isolation.
More and more tiny home communities are popping up across the United States, often in quiet places that feel like true retreats. They represent an appealing alternative to traditional housing, especially for seniors who prefer to age in place, combining the benefits of minimalist living with the convenience of shared spaces and resources.
Kala’s tiny house on wheels is parked in one such community, allowing her to enjoy a simplified life with lower living expenses and a closer connection to nature. Kala’s compact home, which she calls the Turtle Cottage, is located in Tiny Tranquility, a community of more than 40 tiny houses on the Oregon coast, about two miles south of Waldport. It’s very close to the ocean, providing a dreamy coastal setting and the benefit of enjoying nature whenever she wants.
Built on a triple-axle gooseneck trailer, the tiny home is 41 feet (12.5 meters) long and 8.5 feet (2.6 meters) wide, and it was built by Mint Tiny House Company, a well-versed builder based in Vancouver that specializes in custom tiny house RVs, park models, and modern prefab modular homes. Kala purchased it from a previous owner for $145,000 and has been living there full-time with her two cats for the past year.
Photo: Tiny House Giant Journey/YouTube screenshot Finished in green-painted board-and-batten siding, Turtle Cottage fits perfectly into its surroundings. The main attraction on the outside is a spacious back wooden deck with a protective railing. She had it built by a local contractor, and it significantly extends her living space to the outside. It’s large enough to accommodate an outdoor seating arrangement, but the best thing about it is that it offers lovely views of the meadow and the surrounding trees.
The house also has a covered patio directly in front of the main entrance. It is enclosed with protective netting, and Kala turned it into a private catio - an outdoor space where her two cats can safely enjoy some fresh air.
Inside the Turtle Cottage, every nook and cranny serves a purpose, but the living space does not feel cramped or overwhelming. On the contrary, thanks to the glass door and an abundance of windows all the way up to the ceiling that flood the home with natural light, every area feels open and inviting . The white tongue-and-groove pine walls maintain the bright atmosphere, while the natural wood window frames and exposed beams add a tinge of rustic charm.
Photo: Tiny House Giant Journey/YouTube screenshot Given the generous length of the house, there is plenty of space inside for everything needed for full-time living, especially for a single person. The layout includes an open-plan kitchen and living area, a private bedroom over the gooseneck, a separate bathroom, and a large loft.
Centrally located, the kitchen is large and well-equipped. With both floor-based and overhead cabinets, it offers plenty of space for cooking essentials, and everything is cleverly arranged to ensure an easy workflow. Kala confesses cooking is really not her passion, but she has everything she needs for home-cooked meals, including an oven, a three-burner gas cooktop, and a microwave.
The kitchen is also equipped with a large farmhouse sink with a little drainer, a full-size refrigerator, and durable granite countertops.
Photo: Tiny House Giant Journey/YouTube screenshot The living room is not very large but feels snug and intimate, designed for comfort and relaxation. Kala furnished it with a comfortable two-person sofa, a side table, a TV stand with shelves and drawers, and a big cat tree, turning it into a comfortable space for both her and her pets. The high, vaulted ceiling in this area makes it feel a bit more spacious, and all the windows open for fresh air and ventilation.
From the kitchen, a staircase leads up to the loft and a narrow hallway takes you to the bathroom and gooseneck bedroom. The bathroom is located just under the loft, but the ceiling is still quite high, and the room is spacious and comfortable. What’s more, it is fitted with everything needed for full-time living, including a full-size shower with a glass door, a regular flushing toilet, a vanity sink, a washer/dryer machine, and even generous storage.
Four storage steps and a steel handrail make access to the bedroom really easy. The room has all the qualities of a proper bedroom, with full standing height, space to move around the comfortable double bed, a sliding door for privacy, and two massive windows flanking the bed. Drawers on all sides of the bed add a generous amount of extra storage for clothes and other belongings.
Photo: Tiny House Giant Journey/YouTube screenshot As mentioned, Kala’s tiny house also features a loft. It’s actually a very large loft that goes all the way to the front of the house. It can accommodate a mattress or a daybed if she ever wanted to have visitors, but right now, she only uses for storage. The loft is accessed through an L-shaped staircase whose functionality goes beyond just a point of access. Its stair treads lift up to reveal extra storage, and underneath it there is also a slide-out pantry and a coat cabinet.
Kala chose tiny living for the simplified lifestyle and closeness to nature, but it also brought her more financial freedom. For the parking spot in the tiny house community, she pays $872 per month, and that includes all the utilities and the use of the shared amenities.
